scripture: Psalm 63:1-5; Romans 5:12; Romans 3:23; Luke 7:36-39, 44-47; Romans 2:4; Isaiah 26:3
questions: The woman in Luke 7 responded to Jesus with humble love, while Simon responded with pride. Which response feels more natural in our house right now, and why?
Psalm 63 describes thirsting for God the way a dry land thirsts for water. What usually pulls our attention away from God during a normal week?
prayForStudents: Pray students respond to God's kindness with humble gratitude and learn to redirect their focus back to Him in prayer and worship.

guide.summary: This week's message, Redirection, opened our Prayer and Worship series. Students looked at how prayer and worship are part of an ongoing conversation with a personal God, and how they express our dependence on Him and love for Him. Through Psalm 63 and Luke 7, they saw that Jesus restores what sin broke, and that a grateful heart can redirect us back to God when pride or distraction pulls us away.
talkAboutIt: The woman in Luke 7 responded to Jesus with humble love, while Simon responded with pride. Which response feels more natural in our house right now, and why?
Psalm 63 describes thirsting for God the way a dry land thirsts for water. What usually pulls our attention away from God during a normal week?
What is one way our family could use prayer or worship this week to turn our focus back toward God?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Pick one ordinary moment this week (before school, in the car, or after dinner) and practice a short redirection: name one thing God has done, thank Him out loud together, and each share one honest sentence of prayer. Keep it simple and keep going even if it feels awkward at first.
guide.prayer: God, thank You that You welcome us into relationship with You through Jesus. Forgive us for the times we grow proud or distracted. Redirect our hearts back to You, and help our family respond to Your kindness with gratitude and love. Amen.

tryThisAtHome: Pick one ordinary moment this week (before school, in the car, or after dinner) and practice a short redirection: name one thing God has done, thank Him out loud together, and each share one honest sentence of prayer. Keep it simple and keep going even if it feels awkward at first.

questions: Jesus made time to pray alone and with others. When is it easiest for you to talk to God, and when is it hardest?
In the garden, Jesus prayed for the Father's will over His own. Where do you find it hardest to trust God's will right now?
prayForStudents: Pray students grow in relationship with God by making prayer a priority and seeking the Father's will.

guide.summary: This week's message, Relationship, focused on how Jesus modeled prayer. Students saw that He made prayer a priority, sought the Father's will even in hard moments, and gave us a pattern to follow in Matthew 6. The big idea was that prayer helps us grow in relationship with God as we listen, speak, surrender, and ask for help.
talkAboutIt: Jesus made time to pray alone and with others. When is it easiest for you to talk to God, and when is it hardest?
In the garden, Jesus prayed for the Father's will over His own. Where do you find it hardest to trust God's will right now?
Which part of Jesus' prayer pattern (relationship, humility, surrender, or asking for help) do you most want to practice this week?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Try Jesus' prayer pattern together once this week. Slowly pray through Matthew 6:9-13: begin with who God is, ask for His will, then name one need, one place you need forgiveness, and one temptation you want help with. Keep it short and honest.
guide.prayer: Father, thank You that we can come to You through Jesus. Teach our family to make prayer a priority, to seek Your will, and to ask for help with honest hearts. Shape us as we talk with You. Amen.

tryThisAtHome: Try Jesus' prayer pattern together once this week. Slowly pray through Matthew 6:9-13: begin with who God is, ask for His will, then name one need, one place you need forgiveness, and one temptation you want help with. Keep it short and honest.

questions: Everyone worships something. What people, goals, or screens most easily compete with God for your attention?
Who is someone who shows you what God is like just by how they treat people?
prayForStudents: Pray students worship God with their everyday lives and reflect His love in how they treat others.

guide.summary: This week's message, Reflection, reminded students that God created people to know and worship Him. Worship is more than a song set; it is a life that reflects God's image through our actions and how we treat others. Students were challenged to root their identity in belonging to God and to let everyday words and choices become worship.
talkAboutIt: Everyone worships something. What people, goals, or screens most easily compete with God for your attention?
Who is someone who shows you what God is like just by how they treat people?
What is one ordinary thing you do this week that you could turn into an act of worship?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Choose one everyday activity this week (a meal, homework help, chores, or a ride to practice) and treat it as worship on purpose. Before you start, pray together: "God, help us do this in a way that reflects Your love." Afterward, share one way you saw God's goodness in that ordinary moment.
guide.prayer: God, You made us and we are Yours. Help our family worship You with more than songs. Shape our everyday words and actions so they reflect Your love to the people around us. Amen.

tryThisAtHome: Choose one everyday activity this week (a meal, homework help, chores, or a ride to practice) and treat it as worship on purpose. Before you start, pray together: "God, help us do this in a way that reflects Your love." Afterward, share one way you saw God's goodness in that ordinary moment.

questions: Daniel kept a daily time with God for decades while living in a culture that didn't follow God. What makes a daily rhythm with God hard in our house right now?
Daniel 9:18 says Daniel came to God "based on your abundant compassion," not his own good record. How does that change the way we think about the days we miss?
prayForStudents: Pray students build a daily rhythm with God and remember His grace on the days they miss.

guide.summary: This week's message, Rhythms, wrapped up our Prayer and Worship series. Students looked at three rhythms that keep faith growing. From Daniel 9, they saw a man who read God's Word and then prayed it back to God. From Acts 2:42-47, they saw the early church devoted to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer together. From Acts 9 and 1 Timothy 1, they saw how God's mercy met Saul, a man far from Him. The big idea: Grace starts it. Rhythm keeps it. Students were challenged to try the Daniel Window: same time, same place, Bible before apps, read one short passage, and pray one honest line back to God.
guide.keyVerse: "For we are not presenting our petitions before you based on our righteous acts, but based on your abundant compassion." Daniel 9:18 (CSB)
talkAboutIt: Daniel kept a daily time with God for decades while living in a culture that didn't follow God. What makes a daily rhythm with God hard in our house right now?
Daniel came to God based on God's compassion, not his own good record. How does that change the way we think about the days we miss?
The early church in Acts 2 grew in faith together. What is one way our family could make time with God something we do together?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Try the Daniel Window as a family: pick a set time and place, Bible before phones, read one short passage together, and each pray one honest sentence back to God. If you miss a day, just start again. Grace starts it. Rhythm keeps it.
guide.prayer: God, thank You that we come to You because of Your compassion and not because we have it all together. Help our family build a rhythm of time with You. When we miss a day, remind us that Your grace is still there, and help us start again. Amen.

tryThisAtHome: Try the Daniel Window as a family: pick a set time and place, Bible before phones, read one short passage together, and each pray one honest sentence back to God. If you miss a day, just start again. Grace starts it. Rhythm keeps it.

questions: When worry starts piling up, what helps you feel steadier, and how can I help?
Philippians 4 points us to prayer and thanksgiving when anxiety rises. Which of those feels more natural for you, and which feels harder?
prayForStudents: Pray students who feel anxious know God cares, and find steadiness through prayer and gratitude.

guide.summary: This week's message, Anxiety, began The Gospel (Mental Health) series. Students heard that God cares about anxiety, and that prayer, gratitude, and focusing on God and others help put anxiety in its place. They also heard that when worry becomes lasting or life-altering, God can work through wise help like counselors and doctors, and that peace grows as we turn toward Him.
talkAboutIt: When worry starts piling up, what helps you feel steadier, and how can I help?
Philippians 4 points us to prayer and thanksgiving when anxiety rises. Which of those feels more natural for you, and which feels harder?
What is one true, good, or lovely thing you can turn your mind toward when anxious thoughts get loud?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Create a simple family "hand it over" practice. When someone names a worry, pause together: pray it to God in one sentence, thank Him for one good thing you can see right now, and if needed, write down one next step or one trusted adult to talk with. Keep the tone calm and supportive, not rushed.
guide.prayer: God, thank You that You care about our worries. When anxiety feels big, help our family bring it to You with prayer and gratitude. Guard our hearts and minds in Christ Jesus, and give us wisdom to seek help when we need it. Amen.

tryThisAtHome: Create a simple family "hand it over" practice. When someone names a worry, pause together: pray it to God in one sentence, thank Him for one good thing you can see right now, and if needed, write down one next step or one trusted adult to talk with. Keep the tone calm and supportive, not rushed.

questions: Psalm 42 shows someone being honest with God about feeling deeply down while still putting hope in Him. Why do you think both honesty and hope matter?
If a friend felt really down for a long time, what do you think would help them most?
prayForStudents: Pray students facing heavy days know they are not alone and can bring despair to God with hope.

guide.summary: This week's message, Depression, continued The Gospel (Mental Health) series. Students saw in Psalm 42 a writer who names deep sadness, even frustration with God, and still chooses to trust Him. The big idea was that we can trust God while experiencing depression and ask Him to turn despair into hope. They also heard that God cares, Christian community can walk with us, and wise help from counselors and other professionals is a gift when sadness lasts a long time or makes daily life hard.
guide.keyVerse: "Why, my soul, are you so dejected? Why are you in such turmoil? Put your hope in God, for I will still praise him, my Savior and my God." Psalm 42:11 (CSB)
talkAboutIt: Psalm 42 shows someone being honest with God about feeling deeply down while still putting hope in Him. Why do you think both honesty and hope matter?
If a friend felt really down for a long time, what do you think would help them most?
What helps you feel less alone when life feels heavy, and how can our family be a safe place for that kind of honesty?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Read Psalm 42:6-11 together in a calm moment. Invite each person (only if they want) to finish one sentence: "Right now I feel..." and "I want to put my hope in God by..." Then name one trusted person outside the immediate moment (a parent, leader, counselor, or doctor) who can walk with your family if sadness feels heavy or lasting.
guide.prayer: God, thank You that You see us in dark and heavy places. Help our family be honest with You and with each other. Teach us to put our hope in You, and give us courage to ask for help when we need it. Amen.

tryThisAtHome: Read Psalm 42:6-11 together in a calm moment. Invite each person (only if they want) to finish one sentence: "Right now I feel..." and "I want to put my hope in God by..." Then name one trusted person outside the immediate moment (a parent, leader, counselor, or doctor) who can walk with your family if sadness feels heavy or lasting.

questions: What helps you feel secure in who you are, even when friendships feel shaky?
prayForStudents: Pray students find secure love in Christ and build healthy relationships from that security.
